data.name: Dhrupad
data.long_meaning: Dhrupad is a Sanskrit word derived from the roots ‘dhru’ meaning ‘established’ and ‘pad’ meaning ‘sound’. In Hindu mythology, Dhrupad is the name of a renowned singer in the court of Lord Krishna. He was known for his melodious voice and spiritual songs that moved the gods.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that resonates with the divine melody of the universe.

in_sanskrit.name: धरुव
in_sanskrit.meaning: धृत् पद् - fixed, established, steadfast or immovable
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: धृत् (dhrit) - that which is held, established, firm, steady, fixed, unchangeable. पद् (pad) - foot, step, base, foundation. Therefore, Dhrupad means 'that which is fixed or established at the base or foundation'. This is the origin of the name in Sanskrit.

in_tamil.name: திருப்பத
in_tamil.meaning: திரு (thiru) - sacred, divine, holy. பதம் (patham) - base, foundation. Therefore, Dhrupad in Tamil also means 'sacred or divine base or foundation'. This is the origin of the name in Tamil.

data.cultural_impact: Dhrupad is an ancient Indian classical music genre that originated in the 13th century. It is characterized by its slow tempo, intricate rhythms, and complex vocal techniques. Dhrupad is respected for its rich cultural heritage and is a significant contribution to Indian music. It continues to be passed down through traditions and has influenced the development of other Indian classical music styles.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mythology, the name Dhrupad is also associated with spiritualism and devotion. Dhrupad, the divine singer, is believed to have created music that touched the hearts of the gods and founded the genre of Dhrupad music. His songs were thought to carry the power to evoke emotions, cultivate peace, and bring people closer to their spiritual side. Thus, the name Dhrupad embodies the essence of both musical excellence and spiritual enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Dhrupad originated in the 13th century as a courtly music style in the Mughal Empire of India. It was performed by professional musicians employed by the royal courts.

The name 'Dhrupad' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'dharu' which means 'base' or 'foundation'. This refers to the strong rhythmic foundation that is a characteristic feature of this classical music genre.
